name: Gas-heated reforming
principle: A gas-heated reformer uses the hot syngas leaving an autothermal reformer (ATR) to heat the steam-reforming reaction, so most of the heat needed comes from the process rather than a fired furnace. The GHR+ATR combination makes syngas for hydrogen with one concentrated CO2 stream that can be captured at 95% or more. IEA rates ATR with a gas-heated reformer at TRL 5.
